client_alerts.headline: OpenAI Daybreak Blue: personal-account sessions become training data starting Nov 29
client_alerts.body: Forum posts quote an OpenAI email saying that from **November 29** onward, OpenAI may use content from Daybreak Blue sessions on personal paid accounts to improve its models. Nobody has found an opt-out, and it is unclear whether content submitted before the cutoff is covered. The change was first reported earlier this week; the date in the email is Sunday, not Saturday as previously reported. Any client staff running security or DR work through a personal Daybreak Blue account should move to a business workspace or stop by tomorrow. The reports are secondhand, so check them against the email itself.

top_moves.title: Nov 30 deadline cluster: Sonnet 4.5 retires, Opus 4.8 fast mode ends, Gemini 4 Argon API price doubles
top_moves.body: Three changes land on Monday. Anthropic retires **Claude Sonnet 4.5** and removes fast mode for **Opus 4.8**. The introductory **Gemini 4 Argon** API price ($2 / $10 per million tokens) ends and is reported to rise to **$4 / $20**. Any client automation or runbook tooling pinned to these model IDs needs a model swap or a budget check before Monday.

top_moves.title: GPT-6.2 Astra users hit usage limits about 40% sooner after OpenAI fixes a pricing error
top_moves.body: A weekly roundup reports that OpenAI patched an Astra metering error, which in effect cuts the usable quota on the merged Chat and Work meter. Heavy drafting sessions will run out sooner than they did last week.

top_moves.title: Unconfirmed rumors that a lab has cracked polynomial-time factoring put RSA on the watch list
top_moves.body: On Nov 24, Scott Aaronson wrote that he had heard 'many rumors' of OpenAI or Anthropic factoring in polynomial time. No lab has confirmed it. Separately, Google's Cogentic multi-agent proof system released six theoretical papers. Treat both as watch items. Clients can use the noise to justify starting a post-quantum and crypto-agility inventory.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Astra limits now run out about 40% faster after a metering fix; Daybreak Blue training use starts Nov 29.
providers.detail: Reports say a patched pricing error means GPT-6.2 Astra users hit their limits about 40% sooner. The Daybreak Blue change (personal-account sessions may be used for training) takes effect Nov 29, with no opt-out found. Private Inference testing for business customers continues from earlier this week.
providers.alertReason: Daybreak Blue personal sessions become training data on Nov 29

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Claude Ship code-review agents are in beta (Nov 23); Sonnet 4.5 retires and Opus 4.8 fast mode ends Nov 30.
providers.detail: Claude Ship is a suite of agents that review and approve code, for GitHub-hosted Team and Enterprise customers. Monday's deprecations, Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.8 fast mode, are the near-term action item. Fable 5.2 ($8 / $40), Claude Meetings beta and Desktop release channels are earlier November items still settling in.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: The introductory Gemini 4 Argon API price is reported to double on Nov 30; Wallet now connects to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.
providers.detail: The introductory API price for Argon ($2 / $10) is reported to end Nov 30. Reports also say Carbon is now available to all users and Hydrogen replaces Flash, though sources conflict. The Google Wallet link to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode is opt-in.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Still no Grok 5; Grok 4.7 and Voice 3.0 remain current.
providers.detail: Nothing new this week. The last change was the Nov 2 retirement of grok-imagine-image-quality.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new release; Muse Ember (Nov 9) and Muse Glimmer (Apache 2.0) are current, and the Muse Spark 1.2 weights are still promised.
providers.detail: Llama 4 is still the last Llama-branded model. Zuckerberg's promise to release the Muse Spark 1.2 weights has no date.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release; on-prem Managed Agents were due in late November and still haven't been confirmed.
providers.detail: An aggregator lists Mistral Large 4 from Nov 2, but there is no primary announcement. Watch for on-prem agents before month-end.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No new release; Teammates (Max only) is current and the Amazon cease-and-desist over Comet is unresolved.
providers.detail: Nothing new since the Nov 6 release covering Teammates, local Computer on Mac and Voice mode.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: No new post-Ignite changes; Skills and the worldwide rollout of shared Chat and Cowork history continue through November.
providers.detail: Connector write actions are GA in Copilot Chat and Cowork. Autopilot timing for Frontier tenants depends on Message Center.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No confirmed late-November update; Anthropic's Claude Ship now competes directly for code review.
providers.detail: Usage-based billing (since June) and Agent Plugins 1.0 are current.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: The reported Nov 12 cutoff of OpenAI models is still unconfirmed; Claude supply continues.
providers.detail: Cursor 3.24 (Oct 9) is the latest confirmed version.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No November release; Gamma 5 (Oct 6) is current.
providers.detail: Context sources such as Slack and Notion arrived in the Gamma 5 cycle.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release; the Oct 19 update (Agents, BYOK, credit system) is current.

month_themes.now: Model retirements and price increases at month-end, training-data scope creep (Daybreak Blue), and quotas tightening on flagship models (Astra)

Keep using Claude for long-document synthesis. If you batch-process standards through the Gemini 4 Argon API, run the jobs before the Nov 30 price rise or switch to Hydrogen.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Add the **Daybreak Blue** training change and **model-retirement dependency** to the AI third-party risk checklist. Retirements on hard dates are a continuity risk for any AI-dependent workflow.
